newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's PP aims firm words at ETA on anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Spain's PP aims firm words at ETA on anniversary.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar told party supporters on Monday he would not be pressured by ETA rebels into making concessions to the separatists.
"I am not prepared to accept any kind of pressures. The government does not take politics as an arm-wrestling match," Aznar said in a clear message to ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) guerrillas.
A copy of his address to supporters in Avila celebrating the ruling Poipular Party's election victory one year ago was made available to Reuters in advance.
ETA has been blamed by the government for killing six people so far this year including a supreme court judge.
People close to the group have said the ETA was frustrated at the government's refusal to negotiate the end of a 29-year campaign for an independent state. About 800 people have been killed.
Aznar's government has rejected any talks unless the rebels lay down their arms.
Earlier, government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez said creating jobs was the top objective this year and fighting ETA as the second priority.
"The struggle against unemployment is the principal issue of this year...and the struggle against the terrorists is the second big objective of the government," Rodriguez told reporters.
The PP was highlighting its economic programme as the crowning achievement after 13 years of Socialist rule.
An austere 1997 budget aimed at placing Spain among the founders of a single European currency in 1999 has cheered financial markets.

But while inflation has fallen to its lowest level in 28 years and interest rates are also at historically low levels, little headway has been made in reducing western Europe's highest unemployment rate at almost 22 percent.
